name: Habban ibn Hilal
nameAr: حبان بن هلال الباهلي، ويقال الكناني، أبو حبيب، البصري

orthography.spelled: Habban, with fathah on the ha' and a doubled ba'
homographs: Hibban ibn Musa (with kasrah), who never met Hammam
orthography.source: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 7, on those named Habban; Taqrib al-Tahdhib, section on Habban with fathah

diedNote: 216 AH (Taqrib); the Shamela record also gives 210

students.name: Zuhayr ibn Harb, Abd ibn Humayd and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi
students.nameAr: زهير بن حرب وعبد بن حميد والدارمي

verdicts.via: Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Asadi
verdicts.en: With him ends the line of verification in Basra.

verdicts.ar: كان ثقة ثبتا حجة، وكان امتنع من التحديث قبل موته
verdicts.en: He was reliable, firm, a proof; he refrained from narrating before his death.

verdicts.ar: ثقة مأمون على ما يحدث به
verdicts.en: Reliable, trustworthy in what he narrates.

verdicts.source: al-Talkhis, as quoted in Ikmal Tahdhib al-Kamal 3/340

dhahabi.source: al-Kashif, as given on the Shamela record

flags.label: Not Hibban ibn Musa
flags.detail: Ibn Hajar: “Habban narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us” is Habban with fathah, Ibn Hilal, not Hibban with kasrah, Ibn Musa, because the latter never met Hammam (Hady al-Sari, ch. 7). Muslim 2381 gives the full name.

bio: The Basran whom Ahmad named as the end-point of verification in his city, and the most careful of the three students through whom al-Bukhari records the cave hadith from Hammam. His chain in 4663 says “narrated to us” at every link, where the other two routes say “from”. Muslim records the same hadith from him through three shaykhs.

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 7: those named Habban (Wikisource)
